newsitem.title: CUBA: Haitian emigrants repatriated from Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Haitian emigrants repatriated from Cuba.

text.p: Cuba has repatriated 51 Haitian nationals, taking to more than 600 the number of would-be emigrants who have returned to Haiti from Cuba this year, Cuban state media said on Thursday.

The latest group -- 41 men, seven women and three children -- were flown back to Haiti on Wednesday under a voluntary repatriation programme run by the Cuban Red Cross. They had been living since July at a transit camp at Maisi on the easternmost tip of the communist-ruled island.

Similar repatriations took place in February and May. Haitians heading for the United States in boats are often forced to land in eastern Cuba because of bad weather or because their vessels are unseaworthy.
If they cannot continue their journey, Cuban authorities provide them with shelter at Maisi until they decide to return home. Few of the Haitians choose to stay in Cuba.
Since 1980, more than 75,000 Haitian would-be emigrants have received assistance in Cuba, according to Cuban figures.
